Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, it appears that elderly patients are less likely to call 911 in response to clinical scenarios suggestive of acute stroke compared to younger populations. These results suggest that interventions specifically designed to increase awareness of potential stroke signs and symptoms and appropriate subsequent clinical actions may be necessary to address this issue.

In other words, the available data indicate that while many healthcare providers are aware of the importance of recognizing and responding to acute stroke, elderly patients in general may not respond promptly or appropriately when confronted with a potential stroke scenario.
